headline.label: Attax vs Hoiko
headline.detail: one game per seed (seat-swapped replays were identical, so counted once)

tagline: A versus AI for the falling-block game. It won 195 of 200 games against Hoiko, 100 of 100 against intetrigence (derived from MinusKelvin's Cold Clear 2), and 88 of 100 against clys.

copy.claim: In guideline versus rules, across the three measured opponents — Hoiko, intetrigence (derived from MinusKelvin's Cold Clear 2), and clys — nothing tested comes close.
profiles: Hoiko. Hoiko used preset we, beam 150, depth 14 and a 2-piece preview, with adaptation off. Both sides got the same pieces and locked one piece per 120 ms. Seeds 1001–1200 were never used for tuning. Swapped seats replayed the same game, so each seed counts once.

intetrigence. Derived from MinusKelvin's Cold Clear 2. In its own published 100-game eval at 100 ms / 5 PPS, intetrigence beat the official Cold Clear 2 77–23. Here it ran at that same profile, on its own referee (--rules guideline), with Attax connected over TBP. The 50 seeds (5001–5050) were new to both projects, and each was played from both seats. Attax won both games on all 50 seeds. Median think time per move: Attax 35 ms, intetrigence 151 ms.

clys. citrus610's Monte Carlo beam search bot ran its default configuration (width 500, depth 32, branch 3, 1 thread). Seeds 7001–7050 were played from both seats; Attax won 46/42 by seat, with no draws. clys generated more attack per piece; Attax won on survival, clearing 7,948 lines to clys's 6,267. The external-bot referee uses the guideline attack table without combo or perfect-clear attack, 5 previews, hold and 5 PPS paired turns. clys gets a 100 ms search window; Attax completes fixed work without a deadline. Lanes use dedicated CPU cores, with one bot thinking at a time per lane. Neither bot sees pending garbage over TBP. All recorded games were replay-verified.
fairness: intetrigence settings audit. The audit was done before the result was trusted, and it found the harness fair. Attax's search ran to completion on all 14,230 moves. intetrigence used more than its 100 ms target. The two never competed for CPU, and every move was checked by intetrigence's own referee. verify-replay re-ran all 100 games.
Against Attax. TBP carries no garbage information, so Attax played without seeing incoming garbage. intetrigence could see it.
unmeasured: Direct games against the real Hoiko.exe. The benchmark machine has no Wine. The replica matched the .exe on 500/500 moves (seed 1) and 200/200 each (seeds 2 and 7).
Hoiko with its wall-clock adaptation on.
Official Cold Clear 2 itself. That comparison goes through intetrigence, which beat it.
intetrigence at budgets other than 100 ms / 5 PPS, and rules with combo or perfect-clear attack.

clys outside its default configuration, 100 ms window and this rules profile. Its evaluator values combo/perfect clears that the referee does not score. This is not an equal-compute ranking. Attax sees only 20 rows and ignores bag state; clys sees 40 rows and can use bag state. The game-level Wilson interval is descriptive: independent units are 50 seed pairs. Stochastic search and time slicing can change fresh scores. No game reached the 1000-turn cap. Realtime inputs and network latency were not measured.
